name: The One Page
summary: Monday morning at Park Station, on the edge of Golden Gate Park. Detective Ortiz finally has something on paper — a 2018 dissolved-entity records pull that puts {{pc:1}}'s father's signature on a 1994 Argonaut Records Holdings filing, and a seven-year hole nobody thought was worth a phone call. Over coffee in Berkeley, {{pc:3}} reads the negative space in Loewe's excised pages and finds six figures in an arrangement she cannot interpret. In Berkeley, the ranger from Bodie buys her own coffee and tells them almost nothing, warmly. And on an Outer Sunset porch at dusk, in a dark house whose owner has not been seen since Thursday, an index card is wedged in the storm door at eye height with a name and a number on it.
hooks: Two days after Sacramento, and the party is still travelling in two cars — out of habit, because nobody re-negotiated it.
{{pc:1}} caught a discrepancy in the detective's voicemail at the last session. He was right. This is the episode where being right gets him something.
The park ranger's text — 'see you in Berkeley soon' — is the campaign's outstanding promise. Pay it.
inGameDate: Monday, February 2027 — two days after the Saturday of Ep 4
arcBeats: The institutional and personal threads turn out to be the same piece of paper: {{pc:1}}'s father's 1994 signature on an Argonaut filing.
A1 planted — Nia Chen's name reaches the party on an index card in Bea's storm door.
The Ep 4 cliffhanger is paid: Alaia Vega in person, warm, and revealing almost nothing.
